subproblem.title: A map with injective derivative on a Borel set is countably piecewise bi-Lipschitz there
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and B ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel such that H is differentiable at every a ∈ B with injective derivative DH(a) (fderiv ℝ H a). Then there are Borel sets C_l ⊆ ℝⁿ (l ∈ ℕ), pairwise disjoint, with ⋃_l C_l = B, and constants m_l > 0 such that m_l·|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for all l and all a, a' ∈ C_l.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (H : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)), MeasurableSet B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ H a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ H a)) → ∃ (C : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ l, MeasurableSet (C l)) ∧ Pairwise (fun k l => Disjoint (C k) (C l)) ∧ (⋃ l, C l) = B ∧ (∀ l, 0 < m l) ∧ ∀ l, ∀ a ∈ C l, ∀ a' ∈ C l, m l * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖H a - H a'‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the partition step of the parent proof (step 2(d), reused verbatim in its step 7: Mathlib's partition lemma with the radius r(A) := 1/(2K_A) for injective A, then |H(u) − H(v)| ≥ (2K_A)⁻¹|u − v| on each piece).
1. Coercivity constants. If A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is an injective continuous linear map, then ker A = 0 and, ℝⁿ being finite-dimensional, A is K-antilipschitz for some K > 0 (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith): |v| ≤ K|Av| for all v. Put c(A) := 1/K > 0, so c(A)|v| ≤ |Av| for all v. For non-injective A put c(A) := 1. (The choice of K is made once for each A, by choice.) Define the radius r(A) := c(A)/2, an element of ℝ≥0 with r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
2. Partition. For a ∈ B, H is differentiable at a, so H has derivative DH(a) at a within B. Apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := H, s := B, f' := DH and the radius r of step 1 (r(A) ≠ 0 for all A). It gives Borel sets t_l (l ∈ ℕ), pairwise disjoint, with B ⊆ ⋃_l t_l, and continuous linear maps A_l such that (i) |H(a) − H(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ r(A_l)·|a − a'| for all a, a' ∈ B ∩ t_l (ApproximatesLinearOn), and (ii) if B ≠ ∅ then for every l there is y_l ∈ B with A_l = DH(y_l).
3. Pieces. Put C_l := B ∩ t_l and m_l := r(A_l) = c(A_l)/2 > 0. Each C_l is Borel (B and t_l are), the C_l are pairwise disjoint (C_l ⊆ t_l), and ⋃_l C_l = B ∩ ⋃_l t_l = B.
4. Lower bound. Let a, a' ∈ C_l. Then B ≠ ∅, so A_l = DH(y_l) with y_l ∈ B, which is injective by hypothesis; by step 1, c(A_l)|a − a'| ≤ |A_l(a − a')|. By the triangle inequality and (i), |A_l(a − a')| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| + |H(a) − H(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| + (c(A_l)/2)|a − a'|. Hence m_l|a − a'| = (c(A_l)/2)|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')|. ∎
Remark: B = ∅ and n = 0 need no separate treatment (all C_l are then empty, resp. subsets of the one-point space ℝ⁰).

subproblem.title: A map that is C¹ on an open neighbourhood of a compact set agrees near it with a globally Lipschitz C¹ map
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact, O ⊆ ℝ^P open with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O; no assumption on f off O). Then there are g : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) and L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that g is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^P and, for every x ∈ K, g(x) = f(x) and Dg(x) = Df(x) (fderiv ℝ g x = fderiv ℝ f x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K O : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsCompact K → IsOpen O → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (g : Euclid P → Euclid P) (L : NNReal), ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ LipschitzWith L g ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, g x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ g x = fderiv ℝ f x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(c) of the parent proof (the cutoff f̂ := χf with χ = 1 near K and tsupport χ inside O; f̂ is C¹ with compactly supported continuous derivative, hence Lipschitz by the mean value inequality, and f̂ = f near K).
Notation: thickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) < r} (open), cthickening(r, K) := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ r} (closed); tsupport χ := closure{χ ≠ 0}.
1. Room around K. K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put t := cthickening(δ/3, K) (closed) and s := thickening(2δ/3, K) (open). Then t ⊆ s (Mathlib cthickening_subset_thickening', since δ/3 < 2δ/3).
2. Smooth Urysohn function. There is χ : ℝ^P → ℝ of class C^∞ with values in [0, 1], support χ = s, and χ(x) = 1 exactly for x ∈ t (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff for the open set s ⊇ the closed set t). Hence tsupport χ = closure(s) ⊆ cthickening(2δ/3, K) (Mathlib closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ cthickening(δ, K) ⊆ O. The set cthickening(2δ/3, K) is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so χ has compact support.
3. Definition. g(x) := χ(x)·f(x) for x ∈ ℝ^P. Where χ(x) = 0 (in particular off s, hence off O) we have g(x) = 0 whatever f(x) is.
4. g is C¹ on ℝ^P. It suffices to prove that g is C¹ at every point x (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). If x ∈ O: O is an open neighbourhood of x on which f is C¹, so f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt with O ∈ 𝓝 x); χ is C^∞ at x; so g = χ·f is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.smul). If x ∉ O: then x ∉ tsupport χ (step 2), the complement of the closed set tsupport χ is an open neighbourhood of x on which χ = 0, hence g = 0 on it, and g is C¹ at x (a function eventually equal to the constant 0; ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
5. g = f near K. Let x ∈ K. The open set thickening(δ/3, K) contains x and is contained in t, where χ = 1; so g = f on a neighbourhood of x. Therefore g(x) = f(x), and Dg(x) = Df(x) because Fréchet derivatives only depend on the germ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
6. Lipschitz bound. g has compact support (it vanishes off tsupport χ; HasCompactSupport.smul_right), hence Dg has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), and Dg is continuous since g is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). A continuous function with compact support is bounded: there is C with ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). Let L := max(C, 0) ∈ ℝ≥0. By the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le, g differentiable everywhere), g is L-Lipschitz. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves the claim. ∎
Remark: K = ∅ needs no separate treatment (then every δ > 0 works, χ ≡ 0 and g ≡ 0).

subproblem.title: Gram–Jacobian algebra: J_{L∘A} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿJ_A, |α(Ae)| ≤ J_A‖α‖, and a unit orientation of range A equals ±Ae/J_A

subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Let F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz, B ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel and m > 0 with m|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ B, F differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B, and F(B) ⊆ M. Then the map b ↦ ξ(F(b)) is a.e. strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to B, and for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, ξ(F(b)) is a unit orientation of the n-plane range DF(b) (IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient (F b)) (range (fderiv ℝ F b))).

Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient.
1. M is locally Hⁿ-finite in U. For compact C ⊆ U: θ ≥ 1 on M (R.mult_pos), so Hⁿ(M ∩ C) = ∫_{M∩C} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Also M is Borel and M ⊆ U.
2. Tangent planes along the piece. By sibling piece_tangent applied to (U, Y := M, F, B, L, m) — its hypotheses are step 1, the Lipschitz and lower bounds, the differentiability and injectivity of DF on B, and F(B) ⊆ M — for Lⁿ-a.e. b ∈ B, M has the approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b).
3. Orientation at image points. By R.orients, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x. Since F(B) ⊆ M, the same holds for Hⁿ⌞F(B)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). By sibling piece_pullback (second part), it holds at x = F(b) for Lⁿ-a.e. b ∈ B.
4. Identification. For b in the intersection of the conull sets of steps 2 and 3, M has the approximate tangent spaces Q_{F(b)} and range DF(b) at F(b); approximate tangent spaces are unique (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so Q_{F(b)} = range DF(b) and ξ(F(b)) is a unit orientation of range DF(b). This is the second claim.
5. Measurability. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient); let ξ̃ be strongly measurable with ξ = ξ̃ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). Restricting to F(B) ⊆ M and applying piece_pullback, ξ(F(b)) = ξ̃(F(b)) for Lⁿ-a.e. b ∈ B. The map b ↦ ξ̃(F(b)) is strongly measurable (ξ̃ strongly measurable, F continuous hence measurable; StronglyMeasurable.comp_measurable). So b ↦ ξ(F(b)) is a.e. equal on B to a strongly measurable map, i.e. a.e. strongly measurable for Lⁿ⌞B. ∎
